latest_final: The apparent "courses" are not university classes but the courses of a formal dinner. The HKU student was choosing their meal courses in advance from a menu for a dinner event. However, when the dinner took place, the student was not a diner at the table: their role was connected to serving or attending to the meal rather than eating it, so they did not eat the courses that were brought out. Thus, by the end of the evening, all of "their" courses were gone—served and finished—even though the student themselves had not eaten them. The opening's wording makes this sound like an academic course-selection disaster, when it actually describes a dinner where the student chose menu courses but did not get to eat them.
